correctness.rationale: The two-branch push-forward density is nonuniform for 1<b<2 and exactly uniform at b=1,2, so the distinct two-phase gain pairs are classified exhaustively in the stated range. On the pair (2,1), exact identities B^2=id, AB=A, and A=id+B, with A signed doubling, yield the transfer formula P_A x=x/2 and all parity covariances. Pairing adjacent terms gives iterates of A, and their exact covariance sum gives variance m-4/3+4/(3·2^m). A deterministic bound of 2 to iid binary-digit sums proves the central limit theorem. All finite rational symbolic integration assertions in verify.py passed.

value.rationale: The model is a published periodically forced threshold neuron. The result gives a natural exhaustive classification of its exceptional uniform-marginal gain pairs, then proves that identical marginals mask opposite-sign lag-two correlations at the two temporal phases and yields an exact finite-window variance with a Gaussian limit. Together these quantify hidden forcing in time-aggregated outputs. This is a motivated dynamical/statistical phenomenon rather than an arbitrary isolated invariant or a mere renaming of the doubling map.
